subject: Re: Clemson AI — outage request for remediation & compensation

From: Anita Simmons <anita@clemson-ai.com>

Cc: Raj Patel <raj@clemson-ai.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:17:00 -0400
Subject: Production outage 2027-05-31 - request for remediation

Hi Marissa,

Quick note from the operations team — we saw a sustained 48-minute service disruption yesterday (May 31) that impacted several inference endpoints during our daytime traffic window. We lost ~18% of requests and our fallbacks increased latency by ~3x for a subset of services.

This caused customer-visible errors and a handful of failed jobs. Can Redwood propose remediation (credits/extension) and share a short timeline for root cause and mitigation? We need something to present to our leadership tomorrow.

Thanks,
Anita
Director of ProdOps
Clemson AI

-----Original Message Follows (internal summary requested)-----

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Production outage 2027-05-31 - Clemson AI

Folks — forwarding Clemson's note. Can we get the incident timeline and recommended remediation package (credits + trial extension)? They are a mid-market enterprise on a committed plan but still evaluating a larger Dedicated deployment.

Ask: 1) Postmortem timeline 2) Suggested makegood (token credits and/or trial extension) 3) Quick approval path so we can respond by EOD.

Thanks — Marissa
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Jun 1, 2027 at 10:12 AM Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai> wrote:

> Marissa,
>
> Incident summary attached (clemson_incident_timeline.pdf). Short version: a degraded routing table plus a concurrenct autoscaler race caused a subset of GPU pools to temporarily evict active models; fallback routing added cross-region latency and a small rate of 5xxs. Impact: ~48 minutes from 02:12–03:00 UTC, peak error rate 14%, average p99 latency increased from 240ms to ~760ms for affected routes.
>
> Recommended remediation:
> - One-time token credit equivalent to ~5,000,000 tokens (estimated ~$7,500 list value) to compensate request failures.
> - 30-day trial extension of dedicated burst capacity for free (to rebuild trust while they test Dedicated staging).
> - A short-service-credit clause in their invoice for the impacted billing period (0.5x credit on base usage).
>
> I can draft a short proposal (makegood_proposal_v2.xlsx) for sign-off.
>
> Sean
> Customer Success Manager
>
> On Tue, Jun 1, 2027 at 12:06 PM Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai> wrote:
>
> > Team — the recommended credits look reasonable, but per our escalation policy anything >$5k needs manager approval. Also flag: if we grant a 30-day Dedicated trial, ops needs to lock a one-time onboarding slot (we have limited seats).
> >
> > For approval path: propose we get verbal approval from Markus (VP) and then send a DocuSign with the token-credit agreement and trial addendum.

> > Lauren
> > Senior Customer Success

Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 08:32:00 -0400

Markus — quick ask for approval. Summary: incident on 2027-05-31 impacted Clemson AI for ~48 minutes; recommended makegood is:
- 5,000,000 token credit (~$7,500 list value)
- 30-day Dedicated trial extension (one-time onboarding seat)
- Service credit formula: 0.5x on base usage for billing period May 28–June 3 for affected routes

Business rationale: Clemson is evaluating Dedicated and is a potential $150k ARR account; granting a modest credit + trial protects the renewal and accelerates Dedicated adoption.

Attachments: makegood_proposal_v2.xlsx (proposal breakdown)

Can you sign off so we can send to the customer and trigger DocuSign?

Thanks,
Marissa
